principles: Trust boundaries must be enforced by code/tests, not only prose.
Koala CLI remains a workflow client unless an explicit future product decision promotes it to an enforce-mode authority client.
Normal local/off development must continue to work; this milestone should prevent overclaiming, not block all local evidence.
Mac/Runner and Python authority ownership must remain in their own repos and stories.
drivers: User concern: CLI-only workflow can fabricate process if it is allowed to certify itself.
PD-1 current decision: CLI is thin local/shadow and lacks runner identity, receipt verification, and full envelope fields.
Milestone 1 must be small and reviewable before Runner CLI / authority-backed DONE gates are implemented.

options.name: docs-only clarification
cons: Does not mechanically stop tests or code from overclaiming authority
Fails the process-fact principle that gate-relevant facts need handler/test backing

options.name: full enforce-mode CLI authority client now
cons: Requires runner identity, signing, receipt verification, and full envelope work outside Milestone 1
Risks rebuilding Mac Runner responsibilities inside CLI

options.name: boundary hardening with explicit classification and smoke tests
pros: Adds mechanical protection against authority overclaiming
Preserves Runner/Python ownership for later milestones
cons: Does not yet provide true server receipt-backed DONE
Requires follow-up milestones for Runner CLI and authority-backed gate

chosen: boundary hardening with explicit classification and smoke tests
rationale: This option directly addresses the user concern without pretending Milestone 1 can solve runner execution or server receipts. It makes the CLI boundary visible in docs, code semantics, and tests while preserving PD-1 thin-client scope.

preMortem.scenario: Smoke tests pass but wording still lets agents say CLI accepted=true is production receipt authority.
preMortem.trigger: Warnings or docs use authority/enforce language without local/shadow/thin-client qualifiers.
preMortem.consequence: Future agents overclaim DONE or L2+ evidence based on local JSON.
preMortem.mitigation: Add assertions for explicit non-authoritative classification and no receipt-backed claim in the focused smoke output.

preMortem.scenario: Implementation drifts into full runner/client work.
preMortem.trigger: Developer adds actor keys, signing, full envelope, or Python/Mac contract changes inside Orchestrate.
preMortem.consequence: Milestone 1 becomes too large and duplicates Runner/Python responsibilities.
preMortem.mitigation: Scope contract protects external repos and excludes full FU-1/FU-2/FU-3 implementation; reviewer checks diff.

preMortem.scenario: Local development breaks because off/shadow evidence becomes blocked.
preMortem.trigger: Boundary guard treats all local evidence as invalid instead of advisory/local.
preMortem.consequence: Existing Koala workflows fail without live authority secrets.
preMortem.mitigation: Tests must prove local/off remains usable and classified rather than blocked.

preMortem.scenario: Story claims seven-milestone progress without routing later milestones.
preMortem.trigger: DONE summary only says M1 completed and omits M2-M7 ownership.
preMortem.consequence: Next agent restarts or implements the wrong repo work.
preMortem.mitigation: CHK-004 requires a routing record in summary/docs and no automatic M2 story creation.
